Get started

Running The Living Studio

The chat-first interface, its first run, and the desktop app.

The Living Studio is the conversational GUI for Outcome-Driven Innovation: an interactive Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, WYSIWYG Impact Simulation, and Causal Lineage inspection, paired with an autonomous agent connected to the MCP server.

The Studio runs three ways locally, plus a hosted deployment. All of them serve the same SPA, which talks only to the sidecar on http://127.0.0.1:8100 — the SPA never contacts MCP or the LLM directly.

Architecture#

┌────────────────────────────┐  /api (JSON)  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
│  Living Studio SPA         │ ────────────▶ │  apps/studio-api (sidecar)    │
│  React + TS + Vite         │  /api/chat    │  FastAPI on 127.0.0.1:8100    │
│  (browser or Tauri webview)│ ◀──────────── │  - config / health / canvas   │
└────────────────────────────┘  SSE stream   │  - steps / outcomes (via MCP) │
                                             │  - /api/chat (LLM tool-loop)  │
                                             │  - conversations + PM memory  │
                                             └───────────────┬───────────────┘
                                                             │ MCP (HTTP)
                                                             ▼
                                             ┌───────────────────────────────┐
                                             │  apps/mcp-server :8000/mcp    │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘
                                                             ▲
                                                             │ OpenAI-compatible
                                             ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                                             │  Your local LLM backend       │
                                             └───────────────────────────────┘

Interface#

The Studio opens as a conversation, not a dashboard.

Surface What it does
First-run tour A four-step, skippable welcome on the very first visit: what the studio is, which ambition brought you here, the live state of your sidecar/MCP/model (with inline repair when the model is down), and the first move. The four doors are I have one in mind, My boss handed me a priority, Help me find the next one, and Pressure-test a bet; each starts the matching conversation. Replay it from Settings → Replay the welcome tour.
First run A short conversation in the chat, not a form: what you are building, who feels the problem, the job they are trying to get done, then where it hurts. One question at a time, with a reflection before the next ask, quick replies, and Explore on my own always visible. Skipping is allowed; answers and progress are kept as a draft. Re-open it any time with /start, the home stage's context pill, or Settings.
Hero One rotating headline above the composer: a greeting (time of day, plus your name if you set one in Settings), the product/job you set up, what is already on the canvas, or an intent-first prompt such as What are you trying to win this quarter? It cycles every few seconds and stays still under prefers-reduced-motion.
Starter cards Below the headline, three canvas-aware conversation cards pair a clear next move with a short reason: Sharpen an opportunity, Pressure-test a bet or Find the next opportunity, and Capture what you heard or Name the job. Select one to start that prompt in the thread; the cards disappear once the conversation begins. Opportunity landscape remains a separate, quiet shortcut.
Composer Docked at the bottom of the transcript. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line, Cmd/Ctrl+K focuses it, / opens the command palette, and the paperclip attaches a text file or an image. Files can also be dropped anywhere on the composer or pasted from the clipboard, and each one is shown with a size (and a thumbnail, for images) plus a remove control before it is sent; a file the studio cannot read is refused with the reason instead of becoming a chip that promises content the model will never see. The hint row's Model control lists the ids the configured backend reports and writes the choice through the same Settings store as the Base URL field. The send button becomes a stop button while a reply streams.
Bar The only persistent chrome: home, new conversation, catch-up, live model status, and settings. There is no navigation drawer to compete with the thread.
Rail Above the conversation, and only once the thread has produced something: Landscape · N, Job map · N, Evidence · N, What I know · N. Every item is derived from the canvas and the memory, so the strip is a record of the work rather than a fixed menu.
Lens A view docks to the right of the thread on wide screens and becomes a full-height sheet on narrow ones. The transcript and the composer stay on screen and stay usable; Esc, Close, or the rail chip closes it. Every lens ends in one sentence that re-enters the conversation — Ask which to chase, Walk me through the job, Weigh the evidence — so leaving a view is never a return to a menu. Settings and catch-up use the same lens.

Replies render Markdown (headings, lists, emphasis, inline and fenced code). While a turn has produced no text yet, an activity line names the phase (Waking the model, Opening your studio tools, Thinking) with a shimmer and an elapsed hint; the phase is announced once to assistive technology, and the reply is marked busy until it settles so a screen reader reads the answer, not every token. Reasoning sits above the answer in a disclosure that opens while it is being written and collapses to Thought for Ns afterwards, and every tool call is a trace chip with the source the turn actually read.

Slash commands#

Type / to open the palette. Up/Down move, Enter or Tab runs the selected command, Esc closes it. Commands are handled in the SPA and never call the model, so they work when it is offline.

Command Effect
/help Every command, as a notice in the transcript
/start Resume the context conversation
/new New conversation
/home Return to the empty stage
/jobs Job summary, then the job map
/landscape, /jobmap, /evidence, /settings Open that lens beside the conversation
/impact, /capture Start the conversation that produces the card. /capture falls back to the offline form when no model answers.
/status Model, MCP, context, and canvas status

Unknown commands produce a transcript notice pointing at /help.

The welcome tour#

The tour is the front door, the context conversation is the first room. It is skippable at every step (Skip the tour or Escape), resumable (progress is stored after every transition in localStorage["studio.onboarding"]), and replayable from Settings.

Everything lives in apps/studio/src/onboarding/:

File Role
content.ts Steps and goal copy as typed data — the only place the words live
machine.ts Pure state transitions, no React or storage
storage.ts Versioned, defensive localStorage persistence
OnboardingProvider.tsx Auto-open, persistence, replay
FirstRunWizard.tsx, steps.tsx, onboarding.css The dialog
../features/flags.ts The firstRunWizard toggle

App.tsx only wires the provider and the wizard around the existing shell; the chat, canvas, and sidecar code are untouched.

Toggling the tour#

firstRunWizard defaults to on. Resolution order, highest first:

Source Example Use
Query parameter ?flags=firstRunWizard:off QA a build without rebuilding
Local override localStorage["studio.flags.firstRunWizard"] = "off" Per-browser opt-out
Build environment VITE_STUDIO_FIRST_RUN_WIZARD=off npm --prefix apps/studio run build Ship it dark
Default on

Accepted values are 1/0, true/false, on/off, yes/no, and enabled/disabled. With the flag off, no dialog renders, no onboarding state is written, and Settings hides the replay action.

Guidance, not gates#

The setup conversation is a nudge, never a prerequisite. If you skip it, the home stage keeps a dashed Tell me what you're building pill; it reopens the conversation exactly where you left off. /start and Settings do the same. The conversation also understands a natural reply: say "skip", "not now", or "show me the landscape" and it reacts instead of recording it as an answer. When a brief exists, it opens on a review and asks what changed rather than asking everything again.

Without a model#

When the LLM is unreachable the Studio keeps working:

  • A Working by hand strip explains the state and offers capture, job map, and context.
  • Messages still return deterministic ODI guidance from the sidecar, labelled Local guidance.
  • Jobs can be created, renamed, and deleted; steps added, edited, and removed; outcomes recorded, re-scored, and removed. All of it goes through the same local repository the model uses.
  • Settings → Base URL and Model reconnect the assistant whenever you are ready.

The user's context is sent with every chat request, so the assistant starts from the product, audience, job, and problem rather than asking for them again.

The thread is the room#

Capture, scoring, simulation, and decisions are conversations. The storefront never asks the PM to leave the thread to do work: the agent asks for the customer's words or the bet in plain language, then renders the surface that carries it. A lens exists for reading and for people who prefer a click, not for doing the work.

That is also enforced in the agent's system prompt: it is told to keep every artifact in the conversation, never to send the PM to a panel, and to end each reply with the next move as an action on the surface.

The conversation runtime#

The transcript is not a hand-rolled message list. It runs on assistant-ui, a React runtime for streaming assistants, bound to the Studio's own store with useExternalStoreRuntime, so the thread gains real conversation capabilities without giving up the message model the sidecar already understands.

Capability What it means here
Streaming delta frames append to the open prose part; the send button becomes stop. Before the first token, the last message shows the current phase with a shimmering label and dots. When you scroll away during a reply, a keyboard-accessible Latest message control returns you to the live end without interrupting assistant-ui's follow behavior. Empty-thread starter cards pair each suggested move with its reason, then give way to the conversation after the first turn.
Reasoning reasoning frames render in a disclosure that starts open while the model is thinking, then reads Thought for Ns and can be reopened. Never persisted, never counted as the answer.
Tools Each MCP call is a trace chip with its status and a short preview of what came back.
Approval A writing tool (add_, create_, update_, delete_, ingest_, remove_) pauses the turn until you answer Allow or Decline. A decline is a tool result, not an error: the model is told no and may propose something else.
Sources Every tool call that returned data emits a source, titled with the tool and a preview. Provenance is what the turn actually read; a citation is never invented.
Attachments Attach from the paperclip, by dropping files on the composer, or by pasting a screenshot. The composer describes accepted text-like files (.md, .mdx, .json, .csv, .yaml, .yml, .log, text/*) and images (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF, at most 5 MB); a drop or paste of anything else is refused with the reason. Chips show a name, size, an image preview, and a remove control. Text is extracted in the browser, capped at 20,000 characters, and sent with the turn. Nothing is stored server-side.
Model The hint row's picker asks the sidecar (POST /api/models) which ids the configured backend serves, keeps the configured model selectable even when the backend omits it, and saves the choice through saveSettings, so Settings and the composer never disagree. An unreachable or empty backend is explained in the menu rather than shown as an empty list.
Branching Edit a user turn or Regenerate a reply and both versions are kept as siblings. Alternative 2 of 3 with ‹/› steps between them, and the visible branch is saved as the conversation's head_id, so a reload reopens the branch you were reading.
Suggestions The empty-stage pills are chosen from the canvas and handed to the runtime as suggestion prompts.
Generative UI A validated UiNode travels as an assistant-ui data part (data-odi-surface) and renders through the same UiRenderer. The catalog stays ours and server-validated.
Voice Deliberately not wired yet. The seam is adapters.dictation plus ComposerPrimitive.Dictate: no backend change and no message-model change. It waits because Tauri's WebKit webview support for the Web Speech API is uneven, and a microphone button that works in only one shell is worse than none.

Where the bridge lives#

File Role
apps/studio/src/assistant/convert.ts The only mapping between ChatMessage/ChatPart and assistant-ui parts, in both directions. Pure, and tested without a runtime.
apps/studio/src/assistant/StudioRuntime.tsx useExternalStoreRuntime: onNew, onEdit, onReload, onCancel, setMessages, onRespondToToolApproval, suggestions, attachments.
apps/studio/src/assistant/attachments.ts The attachment adapter and the browser-side text/image extraction.
apps/studio/src/assistant/parts.tsx One renderer per part: text, reasoning, tool (with its approval), source, file, generated surface.
apps/studio/src/components/chat/Conversation.tsx MessagePrimitive.Parts, the branch picker, the action bar, and the in-place edit composer.
apps/studio/src/components/chat/ThreadComposer.tsx ComposerPrimitive plus the slash palette, connector chips, attachment drop/paste, and attachment-format/size guidance.
apps/studio/src/components/chat/ModelPicker.tsx The composer's model listbox: opens the sidecar's /api/models, keeps the configured id selectable, and saves through Settings.

The sidecar remains the source of truth for what happened. Its additions are opt-in and additive: reasoning, source, and approval stream events; attachments and approvals on /api/chat; GET /api/conversations/{id}/tree; PATCH /api/conversations/{id}; and POST /api/models, which lists the configured backend's ids without raising when it is offline. A client that sends none of these sees exactly the stream it saw before, which is what the CLI and older clients do.

The approval gate is per-process and single-user by design. ApprovalRegistry waits on an asyncio future, POST /api/approvals/{id} answers it, and a timeout (300 s) or a cancelled turn resolves as a declined write, so a turn can never hang and a double click can never run a tool twice. That is the right size for a loopback sidecar with one person at the keyboard; it is not a durable job queue, and it is not pretending to be one.

Extending the conversation#

A new kind of part is added in exactly two places — the mapping in convert.ts and the component in parts.tsx — and then registered in the components map in Conversation.tsx. Do not add a second message list, and never let an unknown part reach the screen as JSON: the converter drops what it does not understand on purpose, and convert.test.ts holds that line.

What it remembers#

The studio keeps a small, local, editable model of the person it is helping. It is not a profile and not a transcript index; it is the handful of things that change the next answer.

Kind What it captures
career The PM's role, remit, and what success looks like for them
opportunity The opportunity or bet currently in play
business Goals, metrics, and commercial constraints
stakeholder Who else matters and what they care about
constraint Time, budget, policy, or technical limits
evidence What has actually been heard or measured
preference How the PM likes to work and be spoken to

Each note is suggested or confirmed. Suggested notes appear first under What I know with Yes, that's right, That's not it, and Edit; confirmed notes can be edited or forgotten. The PM can also add a note by hand. Nothing is silently promoted: the agent may propose, but the person decides.

The agent writes notes through a remember tool during a normal reply. The sidecar applies it, emits a memory SSE event, and the panel updates without a refresh. Memory writes are best-effort — a database failure never turns a good answer into an error.

Storage is a separate SQLite file from the ODI repository: ~/.agentic-odi/studio.db, overridable with AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB (:memory: is supported and is what the tests use). The API is small:

Method Path Purpose
GET /api/memory/observations Everything the agent believes
POST /api/memory/observations Add a note by hand
PATCH /api/memory/observations/{id} Edit text, confidence, or status
DELETE /api/memory/observations/{id} Forget one note
DELETE /api/memory Forget all notes and conversations

Forget everything is a two-step confirmation and also clears the visible thread, because the server deletes the conversations behind it.

The thread comes back#

Conversations are stored beside the memory. On launch the SPA asks GET /api/conversations/latest, restores that thread's user and assistant turns, and continues with the same conversation_id on the next message. New conversation starts a fresh one without touching the memory; Forget everything removes both. The composer stays usable while the restore is in flight, and a restore failure simply leaves the room empty.

Rich responses#

The copilot does not only talk. When a surface carries the evidence better than a paragraph, the agent renders one inline in the conversation: a scored outcome, a ranked opportunity board, a before/after simulation of a bet, a customer quote with its lineage, the eight-stage job map, an opportunity thesis, or a decision record. Three properties keep this safe and cheap to extend:

  • The catalog is closed and owned by the SPA. apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts declares nine primitives and seven cards, their JSON Schema props, and the description the model reads. There is no HTML, no eval, and no third-party component in the path. Prose is rendered by the same Markdown component the transcript already used.
  • The sidecar is catalog-agnostic. The SPA sends the catalog with each turn; the sidecar derives the render_ui tool schema from it, validates what comes back, and streams a ui SSE event. Invalid props return to the model as a tool result naming the exact violation, and the loop offers the tool again, so a fumbled prop is corrected in the same reply. A client that sends no catalog never sees the tool.
  • Cards are views, never actors. Every button is an intent string that the agent receives as the user's next message — one authority, one audit trail.

A surface is one node tree, streamed as one event:

{
  "type": "outcome-card",
  "props": {
    "id": "O-1",
    "statement": "Minimize the time it takes to propagate secrets across environments",
    "importance": 9,
    "satisfaction": 3
  }
}

The opportunity thesis is the intent-first card: one opportunity with its importance, satisfaction, the gap in plain words, the thesis itself, and the smallest next move. It is the shape the agent reaches for when the PM is deciding what to chase, rather than when they are inspecting a single score.

The conversation keeps the order the agent produced: a delta appends to the open prose part, a ui event opens a card, and the next delta opens a new paragraph after it. The opportunity score is computed from importance and satisfaction when the agent omits it, so the ODI formula has exactly one home (src/lib/odi.ts). Unknown component types degrade to a quiet fallback; a tree that fails validation is dropped whole, and the surrounding prose still reads.

Adding a surface#

  1. Add an entry to CATALOG in apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts — props as a JSON Schema subset, plus the description the model will read.
  2. Register the component in apps/studio/src/ui/registry.ts.
  3. Implement it in apps/studio/src/ui/cards.tsx (domain shape) or apps/studio/src/ui/primitives.tsx (composition).
  4. Run npm --prefix apps/studio test. The registry parity test fails if the catalog and the registry drift apart.

No server change is needed, and no new dependency.

Hosted (experimental)#

The built SPA is also served from Cloudflare Workers at https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/. The UI loads without a backend; canvas data, chat, and mutations need the local sidecar and MCP server. Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. See Deployment for the Worker setup.

1. Web — production build (recommended for a quick look)#

npm --prefix apps/studio run build   # build the SPA into apps/studio/dist
python scripts/dev.py            # starts MCP :8000 + sidecar :8100
Service URL
MCP Server http://localhost:8000/mcp
Living Studio http://127.0.0.1:8100

python scripts/dev.py starts both processes concurrently; press Ctrl+C to stop both.

2. Web — dev with hot reload#

Vite proxies /api to the sidecar:

npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full   # MCP + sidecar + Vite together
# open http://localhost:5173

3. Desktop — Tauri 2#

The app spawns the MCP server and sidecar itself:

npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev     # dev window
npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri build   # bundles: .deb / .AppImage (Linux), .app / .dmg (macOS), .msi / .exe (Windows)

[!NOTE] Tauri prerequisites. The desktop build needs the WebKitGTK toolchain and Rust 1.90+. On Debian/Ubuntu:

sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential pkg-config curl wget file \
  libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf xdg-utils libfuse2t64

The Tauri CLI ships as the @tauri-apps/cli npm dev dependency (npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri). The sidecar is launched with uv run python -m … from the repository root; if the app cannot locate the repo root, set AGENTIC_ODI_REPO_ROOT.

Desktop signing & updater secrets#

Self-updating and code signing are env-driven: if a secret is absent, an unsigned artifact is produced instead of failing. CI reads these from GitHub Actions secrets.

Secret Purpose
TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY Signs updater artifacts (.sig) and the latest.json manifest. A tagged release fails loudly without it. Generate with npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate.
TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD Password for the private key (optional when the key has none).
APPLE_CERTIFICATE / APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD macOS Developer ID certificate (base64 .p12) and its password.
APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY macOS signing identity.
APPLE_ID / APPLE_PASSWORD / APPLE_TEAM_ID macOS notarization credentials.
WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE / WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD Windows Authenticode PFX (base64) and its password; imported by CI and injected into the bundle config.

Releases are published by .github/workflows/tauri-release.yml when a v* tag is pushed. The desktop app checks for updates on startup and via Settings → Check for updates.

Managing the updater signing key#

The updater key pair authenticates release artifacts so an installed app can verify that an auto-update genuinely came from you. The public key is embedded in apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json (plugins.updater.pubkey) and is safe to commit. The private key must never be committed, logged, printed in CI, or attached to a build artifact.

  1. Generate a key pair (only if you need a new one). Leave -p "" for a passwordless key, or pass a password and remember it:

    npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri signer generate -- -w ./living-studio.key -p "" -f

    This writes living-studio.key (private, 0600) and living-studio.key.pub (public).

  2. Paste the public key into apps/studio/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:

    {
  "plugins": {
    "updater": {
      "endpoints": ["https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/latest.json"],
      "pubkey": "<contents of living-studio.key.pub>"
    }
  }
}

  3. Store the private key outside the repository (the repo root is git-tracked; a sibling directory is not), with restricted permissions:

    mkdir -p ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys && chmod 700 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys
mv living-studio.key ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/
chmod 600 ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key

    Move it to a long-term secret store (password manager, 1Password/Bitwarden/ Vault, or a private encrypted backup) when you decide where that lives. Losing it means future releases can no longer be signed for existing installs.

  4. Add the private key as a GitHub Actions secret (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret), or via the CLI:

    gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY < ~/repos/agentic-odi-keys/living-studio.key
gh secret set TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD --body ""   # only if you set a password

  5. Verify the secrets exist (values are never displayed):

    gh secret list

  6. Rotate by repeating steps 1–4, then publishing a release signed with the new key. Existing installs still verify against the public key compiled into their binary, so keep the old private key usable and publish the new public key ahead of the cut-over.

[!CAUTION] If the private key leaks, treat auto-updates as compromised: generate a new pair, rotate the Actions secret, and publish a freshly signed release.

Connecting an LLM#

The Studio needs an OpenAI-compatible LLM backend with tool-calling support to drive the agent. For a fully local setup, see Local LLM Backend.

Agent-Driven Testing#

Type /dev in the AI assistant to trigger the full automated workflow: it starts both processes, opens the browser, sends a test message, and reports the results.

Type /test to have the agent run all tests and report the results automatically.
